entries.title: Building AI on credit: structures and spillovers
entries.description: Capital expenditure to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is growing fast, and a rising share is financed with long-term debt and through complex off-balance sheet arrangements.

entries.title: Chokepoints in global supply chains: lessons from rare earths and hard disk drives
entries.description: Concentration and limited substitutability can turn the efficiency gains from global supply chains into vulnerabilities. However, the consequences of chokepoints depend on their underlying nature.

entries.title: News shocks and inflation:  theory and evidence from  large oil discoveries
entries.description: We study hownews shocks affect inflation in open economies, using large oil and gas discoveries with realized production lags of at least five years as observable news about future output. Panel local projections show that discoveries raise core consumer prices over the subsequent decade, with about half the increase occurring prior to extraction.

entries.title: Bank liquidity regulation and the growth of private credit
entries.description: We study the role of bank liquidity regulation in the growth of private credit. Following the introduction of the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), private credit increases significantly more in U.S. counties with a larger footprint of banks subject to the LCR or of LCR banks with greater initial liquidity shortfalls.

entries.title: Inflation after the Iran war
entries.description: An unexpected increase in energy costs raises inflation directly through flexibly-set prices. Whether that shock amplifies to a larger and persistent rise in inflation depends on its transmission through the economy.

entries.title: Competing rails for crossborder payments: banks, fintechs, and stablecoins
entries.description: Cross-border payments remain slow and expensive despite significant improvements in digital financial infrastructure over the past several decades.

entries.title: Geoeconomic pressure
entries.description: The increasing use of geoeconomic pressure is reshaping the global economy.

entries.title: Central banks and macro financial stability in a fragmented global economy
entries.description: The 25th BIS Annual Conference took place in Basel, Switzerland on 26 June 2026. The event brought together a distinguished group of central bank Governors, leading academics and former public officials to exchange views on the theme “Central banks and macro-financial stability in a fragmented global economy”.

entries.title: Offshore forwards and exchange rate transmission in emerging markets
entries.description: We study how offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) markets transmit exchange-rate pressures to domestic currency markets. Using unique transaction-level data on the universe of centrally cleared NDFs for ten emerging-market currencies over 2013–2025, we show that offshore NDF order flow moves both offshore forward and domestic spot exchange rates and widens the offshore–onshore forward spread.

entries.title: Chokepoint disruptions and their  macroeconomic consequences
entries.description: Rising geopolitical tensions, including trade restrictions and conflicts, are increasingly disrupting global supply chains, posing significant risks at critical chokepoints. Strong substitution effects and the use of inventories have helped to mitigate adverse output effects of chokepoint disruptions, but they often come at the cost of higher input prices. An effective policy response to chokepoint disruptions requires a tailored approach that takes account of the cause, centrality and the private sector’s ability to substitute and draw on buffers.
